name: Stop a tab return restarting the whole applicant walk over and over
request: Stop a tab return restarting the whole applicant walk over and over
checks: npm run check passed end to end: typecheck, build, 416/416 tests (up from 415, one added), validate (31 build files, 4 React entry points, service-worker imports)

new test 'a tab switch cannot restart the same walk forever' pins the bound, the collected-based scoring, that an interrupted run still does not set ranKey, that a real arrival clears the budget and that a deliberate press re-arms it; the pre-existing ranKey assertion was updated for the if-block, not weakened
git diff --check passed; scope is applicants.js and its test only; dist/applicants.js rebuilt and verified to match source; no secrets, no unrelated files
NOT verified against live LinkedIn (rule 17). This defect is pure control flow and provable by reading, but whether it is the reloading the user sees still needs a live run
result: The applicants page restarted the entire walk from the first row on every return to the tab. noteReturnToTab() fires on visibilitychange and its only guard was key === autoRun.ranKey, which is set ONLY when a run reaches COMPLETED - and the tab going hidden is itself what interrupts a run, so switching away and back left ranKey empty and restarted the whole walk, which the next switch away interrupted again, unbounded. Bounded it by progress: a tab-return restart that collects nobody increments fruitlessReturns, and after MAX_FRUITLESS_RETURNS (2) the surface stops restarting that view on a tab switch and says so once in the console. A restart that collects somebody resets it, a genuine arrival (a real change of view, not a tab regaining focus) clears it, and Collect Every Applicant re-arms it outright. An interrupted run still does not set ranKey, so the resume feature is intact.
